items.problem: R13's iter-07(a) addendum states the dead-track rule and S18 enforces it — on one route. The wiki entry template, which has 495 instances and is this site's most numerous surface, violates the same rule by a far wider margin than .home-grid ever did, and no check looks at it. Measured by me at 1440x900 on the shipped build: on /wiki/concept/ai-winter, .entry-facts occupies 228.9-680.8 (451.9px) in a 524px-wide right track at x=772-1296, while .prose runs 228.9-2173.9 (1945.1px) in the left track. The shorter side is 23.2% of the taller, against S18's own 60% floor — and the track is not merely under-filled, it is empty: 1493px of blank column beside the entire body of the page. On /wiki/event/attention-is-all-you-need the ratio is 17.0% (294 / 1733). I sampled 24 entries across the index: 4 render the two-column form (the rest are model records with no prose, correctly single-column), and 3 of those 4 fall below the 60% floor, median 52.5%. Meanwhile .rails — the REFERENCED HERE and APPEARS IN blocks, 156.9px tall — sits BELOW the prose at x=144-752, inside the narrow column, with the wide empty track directly above it. This is I9's defect and I9's opportunity on the same page: the content that belongs in the freed track already exists on the template and is currently stacked underneath the column that has no room for it. Stripe's long-form documentation pages hold a persistent right rail for the full scroll length of the article — the transferring property of Stripe's content is exactly this one, a long body with a short set of structured facts and a set of cross-references, and Stripe populates the rail with the cross-references rather than letting it stop 450px down. This surface stops at 451.9px and then holds 1493px open.

items.prescription: Hypothesis, and it is the move this loop has already accepted once: relocate .rails (REFERENCED HERE / APPEARS IN) into the freed track beneath .entry-facts at the template's existing min-width: 60rem breakpoint, exactly as I9 relocated the home page's doors section into .home-side — a position change in the existing grid, no new content, and cross-references are the natural occupant of a navigation rail beside a body of prose. Whichever lever is chosen, S14 must keep holding — .entry-facts' top edge inside the first viewport at both 1440x900 and 390x844 — and the check must be falsified in both directions: a facts block padded artificially tall should NOT satisfy it (the floor is symmetric for that reason), and a genuinely balanced template should not fire.

items.target: shared design system (app/globals.css: .change-annotation, .span-rule, .badge[data-kind]) and tools/ui-invariants.mjs S20's scope
items.problem: R9's iter-08 addendum — written THIS round, for I31 — states the rule absolutely: '--accent is reserved for hover and focus; a resting border, rule or divider shall never carry it'. S20 was registered to enforce it and asserts over exactly two selectors on one page (.door in .doors, .deltas-strip .delta). Three classes of resting --accent survive outside that scope, in the shipped build, in BOTH themes, with the gate green. (a) .change-annotation on the home page carries border-left: 2px solid --accent at opacity 1, 161.1px tall, on the first and most prominent entry of the changed feed — the single loudest colour mark in the site's main content column, and it marks an editorial annotation whose presence is already unmissable as a paragraph of prose. Light rgb(74,59,212); dark rgb(156,147,255). (b) .span-rule uses --accent as its background at opacity 0.45, 490.4x1px, 4 instances on the home page and 54 on /impossible-routine — 58 resting accent hairlines across two templates, both themes. (c) .badge[data-kind='theme'] on wiki entries carries a 1px --accent border, an --accent tinted background (rgb(236,235,251) light / rgb(35,35,56) dark) and --accent text, 3 instances on the sampled entry — sitting on the same line as 'ACTIVE' and 'STABLE', which are the same class of metadata rendered as unboxed muted text. Two treatments for one object class, on one line, and the boxed three are the loudest thing on a page whose point is its prose. I established the scope gap by falsification rather than by reading the source: `--only S20 --break '.door{border-top-color:var(--accent)}'` fires (1 of 1), while `--break '.change-annotation{border-left-color:var(--accent)}'` and `--break '.span-rule{background:var(--accent);opacity:1}'` both leave S20 green (0 of 1 fired). This is the identical shape as I36's own finding about S17 — the check registered for a rule is narrower than the rule's text — reproduced in the same round that fixed it, on the rule that round wrote. Cross-cutting, all three benchmarks agree: colour is reserved for state and meaning rather than decoration. None of these three encodes a state the page names.
items.evidence: measured by me with Playwright against out/ at 1440x900 in both themes (a full-DOM sweep for computed backgroundColor and four border-*-Colors equal to the resolved --accent, run over 11 routes: / -> P.change-annotation borderLeft x1 and SPAN.span-rule background x4; /impossible-routine -> SPAN.span-rule x54; /wiki/concept/ai-winter -> SPAN.badge all four borders x3; the other 8 routes clean); evidence/current/home--light--1440.png (the vertical accent bar beside 'WHAT IT MEANS'); loops/ui-loop/evidence/iter-08-a-judge/wikientry-1440.png and impossible-1440.png; my own --only S20 --break falsification runs
items.invariant: On every route and in both themes, no element in resting state resolves --accent as a border colour, a background colour or a rule colour — at any opacity — unless that element's own value differs from its siblings' in a way the page names in words elsewhere; and S20's assertion sweeps the whole document for that property on every sampled route rather than testing two named selectors on one page.
items.governing_rule: RULES.md R9 (the iter-08 addendum's own absolute statement, which is broader than the check registered for it) and RULES.md R8's badge clause for (c) specifically — boxed only where the tone differs from the collection's default, and all three theme chips carry the identical tone
items.prescription: Hypothesis: (a) .change-annotation's border-left takes --rule-strong; the annotation is already distinguished by being a block of prose inside a one-line feed and needs no colour to say so. (b) .span-rule takes --rule at opacity 1 rather than --accent at 0.45; it is a hairline flanking a duration label and is currently the only reason --accent appears 54 times on /impossible-routine. (c) the theme chips lose their border and tint and take --muted text, matching the 'active'/'stable' tags they sit beside — if a topic tag is genuinely a different class of object from a status tag, the difference belongs in position or in a label, not in the page's one reserved colour. Then widen S20 from a two-selector comparison to a document sweep: resolve --accent for the active theme, walk every element in <main>, and fail on any resting border, background or outline that matches it, with a declared allowlist for genuinely stateful marks (there are currently none, so the allowlist starts empty and every future entry has to argue for itself). Falsify in both directions on at least two routes: inject an accent border on an unexceptional sibling (must fire), and confirm a hover/focus accent still passes (must not fire) — the second direction is the one that would break if the sweep were written naively over all pseudo-states.

items.target: app/page.tsx home changed feed (.rail-changes .rail-item a.src, app/globals.css) and tools/ui-invariants.mjs S17's route list
items.problem: R8's iter-08 addendum states the clause generally — 'a repeated, non-discriminating value shall not carry the SAME visual weight as a column a reader compares across — bordered or linked or otherwise emphasised — unless its own value differs from the collection's stated default' — and I36 just enforced it on the two surfaces S17 samples. The home changed feed is the third surface with the identical shape and it is worse than either, because there the repeated value is not merely equal in weight to the compared column, it is LOUDER. Measured by me at 1440x900 on the shipped build: .rail-changes holds 24 entries; 24 of 24 carry an a.src whose text is the single identical string 'source', rendered at rgb(74,59,212) (--accent) with text-decoration underline, while the .change-name link on the same row — the model name, the value a reader is actually scanning the feed for — renders at rgb(26,27,34) with the same underline. Dark theme identical in structure: rgb(156,147,255) against rgb(228,228,236). In evidence/current/home--light--1440.png this reads as a coloured column of 24 identical words running down the right side of the feed, pulling the eye away from the names on the left. This is precisely the defect I8 removed from /catalog's Read column at iteration 7 — a per-row provenance link at link weight competing with the columns that discriminate — left standing on the page the site opens with. Linear's mechanism, and the transferring property of its content really does hold here (short uniform single-line rows, one discriminating label per row, a small set of secondary affordances): the highest visual weight in a row goes to the value that differs between rows, and secondary affordances sit at the lowest weight the interaction allows. This row does the reverse.
items.evidence: measured by me with Playwright against out/ at 1440x900 in both themes (24 .rail-changes .rail-item, 24 a.src, 1 unique string 'source', computed colour rgb(74,59,212) light / rgb(156,147,255) dark, text-decoration underline; .change-name computed rgb(26,27,34) light / rgb(228,228,236) dark); evidence/current/home--light--1440.png and home--dark--1440.png; my own falsification run `--only S17 --break '.rail-changes .src{color:#4a3bd4;font-weight:700}'` -> 0 of 1 fired, confirming S17 does not sample this surface
items.invariant: On the home changed feed, a value identical on more than 90% of the feed's entries renders at a lower visual weight than the record link on the same entry — measured as computed colour, with the record link's own ink as the reference — and S17's route list includes the home page's .rail-changes alongside /catalog and /tools.
items.governing_rule: RULES.md R8 (the iter-08 addendum's general clause, whose enforcing check samples two of the three surfaces it governs) and RULES.md R9 ('--accent marks hover and focus, not the resting state of a list or table row' — .src is a resting link inside a list row)
items.prescription: Hypothesis: give a.src the --muted token at rest, keeping the underline, so the link remains unambiguously a link and unambiguously secondary; --accent returns to hover and focus, where R9 reserves it, which also gives the hover state something to say that the resting state does not. Contrast at --muted on both grounds is already exercised elsewhere on the same page and R1's floor must be re-run to confirm it, not assumed. Do NOT remove the link — the per-row source is the same provenance requirement I39 records for /catalog and it is this site's whole editorial claim. Then extend S17's route list to the home feed with the record link as the comparison reference rather than a numeric column, and falsify both ways: .src raised to the record link's ink (must fire) and a genuinely exceptional entry keeping full weight (must not fire).

I closed the gap for this verdict by capturing both routes at 1440 and 390 and by probing 11 routes at 416, 544, 768 and 960 — no page-level horizontal scroll anywhere, and /tools' three-column .listing holds at 768 with pricing at 415.3-476.3px of a 721.9px row — so the finding is a recall defect in the rig, not a defect in the artifact. But a judge should not have to build the evidence it is scoring from, and the next judge will not know to.

items.target: app/blog index template (.rail-posts .rail-item's second track, app/globals.css)
items.problem: R7's iter-08 addendum says what to do when a surface outgrows the shared --measure-list token: give that template its own token, do not widen the shared one. It states the trigger as a title exceeding the 3-line bound. /blog has not exceeded it — it is sitting exactly on it, on every row, and the reader-facing symptom the bound exists to catch is already fully present. Measured by me at 1440x900: .rail-item's second track resolves to 384.0px on every row; all four post titles wrap to exactly 3 lines (S15's own printed headroom line says '3 of 3 — NO HEADROOM'); the list's total width is 500px inside a 1152px shell, leaving 796px of the page empty to the right of it. On the same page and directly above that list, the descriptive paragraph is bounded to --measure (38rem / 608px) — so the page sets its secondary prose 224px WIDER than its primary objects, and a reader's eye meets a full-width explanatory paragraph followed by four headlines broken across three short lines each. This is a hierarchy inversion, not a wrapping preference: --measure-list was sized for a row LABEL (a model name, a wiki term, a category count) and a post headline is a sentence. I30 bound .rail-title to this token at iteration 5 because it was previously 1019px, which was the opposite excess and correctly fixed; the token it landed on is the wrong one for this object. Vercel's mechanism is the relevant one and the transferring property is the object class, not the page: a headline gets a headline measure and a list label gets a list measure, and the two are different tokens because they are different objects, which is what makes the grid's rhythm stay visible across a property rather than collapsing every text object onto one width.
items.evidence: measured by me with Playwright against out/ at 1440x900 (.rail-posts computed width 500px at x=144-644; every .rail-item grid-template-columns '100px 384px'; four .rail-title elements at 3 client rects each; the page lede bounded to --measure = 38rem = 608px, right edge ~752px); evidence/current/index-blog--light--1440.png, in which the lede visibly outruns every headline below it; tools/ui-invariants.mjs S15's own headroom line, '3 of 3 lines allowed on /blog — NO HEADROOM'
items.invariant: On /blog, the post-title column is at least as wide as the widest prose block on the same template, and no post title wraps to more than 2 lines at 1440x900; the token that bounds it is declared for this template rather than shared with the row-label surfaces /wiki, /data and /tools, so widening it cannot re-cap a short label elsewhere.
items.governing_rule: RULES.md R7 (its iter-08 addendum names the template-specific token as the remedy for exactly this case and states the trigger as the bound being exceeded; this item is that the trigger should be the surface's TYPICAL content sitting at the bound, which is what 3 of 3 on 4 of 4 rows means) — and note that R7's iter-05(a) dead-air finding is the thing a naive widening would reopen, which is why the remedy must be a new token and not a raised --measure-list
items.prescription: Hypothesis: declare --measure-title (start at 38rem, matching --measure, so the headlines and the lede share one right edge and the page reads as one column) and use it as .rail-posts .rail-item's second track in place of --measure-list. --measure-list stays at 24rem and /wiki, /data and /tools are untouched, so I32's dead-air drift cannot reopen. R10 follows for free: .rail-posts is width:fit-content as of I35, so its border-top tracks the new row width automatically — verify that it does rather than assuming it, since that is the coupling I35 just landed. S15's bound then drops from 3 lines to 2 with real headroom, and its printed margin should say so. Falsify both directions after the change: a title forced past 2 lines at the new width (must fire) and the track forced measurably below the new cap (must fire on the collapsed branch, not the wrap branch).

items.problem: Unchanged and re-verified. 38 of 40 captures are fullPage images at scroll position 0, so nothing scroll-linked is observable from the set (JUDGE.md L3); the two exceptions are the /catalog 1440 pair, correctly labelled capture:'viewport' with a reason naming #catalog-table-wrap's 732.656px max-height (L5). The cost this round was nine Playwright probe runs: the /blog rail width and its resolved grid tracks, the /catalog Read cell's painted colour, /tools' three column colours, the home page's accent inventory in both themes, the wiki entry's two-column heights across a 24-entry sample, the 390px record's line composition, the 11-route intermediate-viewport sweep, and four --break falsifications. items.target: loops/ui-loop/verdicts (I23's second clause) and RULES.md R12's own floor
items.problem: I23's second clause — 'a record's rendered height does not exceed 120px' at 390x844 on /catalog — is arithmetically unsatisfiable while R12, R8 and S2 hold, and it should be retired with the arithmetic recorded rather than carried forward as blocked on keeper I27. Measured by me at 390x844: a record is 215.9px = 17.6px top padding + 17.6px bottom padding + a 31.2px name line + six 24.9px field lines. The labels are already inline with their values (#catalog-table tbody td { display: flex; justify-content: space-between }), so removing the attr(data-label) generated content — the lever I27 gates and the lever both my predecessor's prescription and this round's decline are built around — would free ZERO vertical space. R12 mandates the model name, input price, output price and lifecycle status per record, which is 31.2 + 3x24.9 = 105.9px of content; add the padding and the floor is 141.1px with every optional field deleted. The padding itself is not slack: S2's own comment records it as the deliberate substitute for the per-row rule R8 forbids at this width, so spending it would reopen a defect the loop already fixed. 120px is below the floor of the loop's own rules on this surface. The decline in the change manifest is correct in outcome and wrong in cause, and a wrong cause left on the record is how the fabricated 'licence' field travelled three documents deep this round.
items.evidence: measured by me with Playwright against out/ at 390x844 (tr height 215.9px, padding 17.6/17.6, th 31.2px, six td at 24.9px each, labels rendered inline via flex space-between); app/globals.css lines ~1350-1420 (the max-width: 33.999rem block, including S2's own comment naming the padding as the separation lever); loops/ui-loop/verdicts/iter-07.json I23; loops/ui-loop/verdicts/iter-08-changes.md (the decline)

items.prescription: Retire I23's second clause the way iter-06 retired R13's occupancy branch: strike the <=120px figure, record in RULES.md R12 that the minimum achievable stacked-record height on this surface is 141.1px under R12's own field floor plus S2's separation padding, and state that any future reduction is a content decision (fewer fields per record) and therefore out of this loop's charter, not a presentation one. Update I27's disposition to note it no longer gates I23 — it remains a genuine unanswered accessibility question about whether the generated labels are announced, worth a real screen-reader session, but nothing else in the queue is waiting on it. The surface's real remaining defect at 390 is unchanged and is I14's territory, not a height bound: 396 records over 86,379px is a findability problem that a shorter record does not solve and pagination or grouping would.

items.problem: Unchanged. The viewport-coupled fidelity detector is keyed to one CSS signature — an element whose computed position is sticky and whose max-height is vh-based — so it catches #catalog-table-wrap, correctly labelled this run, and would assert nothing about a second instance built differently. D9's generalisation is that identity is not fidelity; this detector proves fidelity for one known shape.
items.evidence: loops/ui-loop/evidence/current/manifest.json (only the two /catalog 1440 entries carry capture:'viewport', both citing max-height 732.656px); JUDGE.md L5
items.invariant: The evidence rig detects a misrendering fullPage capture by comparing the rendered image against the page's live DOM geometry, not by matching a CSS signature: for each capture, at least one measured element's live bounding box agrees with its position in the captured image within a stated tolerance.
items.prescription: Replace the signature match with a differential check: capture at viewport size and at fullPage, measure one high-signal element's box live in each, and label the capture 'viewport' whenever the two disagree beyond tolerance. That detects the class rather than the instance, and it shares its evaluate() call with I13 and I44.
